    fn eval_call(&mut self, name: &str, args: &[Expr]) -> Result<RValue, RuntimeError> {
        if name == "printf" {
            return self.eval_printf(args);
        }
        if name == "malloc" {
            // Untyped malloc (not assigned to a struct pointer): model as a
            // 1-cell int heap array. The struct-typed cases are handled at the
            // declaration / assignment / return sites which know the type.
            let id = self.fresh_heap_id("heap");
            self.heap.insert(
                id.clone(),
                HeapObjectRuntime::Array(HeapArray {
                    element_type: BaseType::Int,
                    cells: vec![Scalar::Int(0)],
                }),
            );
            return Ok(RValue::Pointer(Some(Location::HeapCell { id, index: 0 })));
        }
        if name == "free" {
            // No-op in the model; keep the object so the trace stays readable.
            return Ok(RValue::Void);
        }
        if name == "exit" {
            // Stop execution cleanly: unwind all frames via a sentinel error
            // that `run()` recognizes and treats as a successful finish.
            return Err(RuntimeError { message: "__exit__".into(), line: 0 });
        }
        if name == "perror" {
            // Print the message to stdout (we don't model stderr separately).
            if let Some(Expr::StrLit(s)) = args.first() {
                self.stdout.push_str(s);
                self.stdout.push('\n');
            }
            return Ok(RValue::Void);
        }

        let func = *self.functions.get(name).ok_or(RuntimeError {
            message: format!("call to unknown function '{}'", name),
            line: 0,
        })?;

        let mut evaled = Vec::new();
        for a in args {
            evaled.push(self.eval_expr(a)?);
        }
        self.call_function(func, evaled, 0)
    }

    fn eval_printf(&mut self, args: &[Expr]) -> Result<RValue, RuntimeError> {
        if args.is_empty() {
            return Ok(RValue::Scalar(Scalar::Int(0)));
        }
        let fmt = match &args[0] {
            Expr::StrLit(s) => s.clone(),
            _ => String::new(),
        };
        let mut out = String::new();
        let mut arg_idx = 1;
        let chars: Vec<char> = fmt.chars().collect();
        let mut i = 0;
        while i < chars.len() {
            if chars[i] == '%' && i + 1 < chars.len() {
                let spec = chars[i + 1];
                i += 2;
                if spec == '%' {
                    out.push('%');
                    continue;
                }
                let val = if arg_idx < args.len() {
                    let v = self.eval_expr(&args[arg_idx])?;
                    arg_idx += 1;
                    v
                } else {
                    RValue::Scalar(Scalar::Int(0))
                };
                match spec {
                    'd' | 'i' | 'l' => out.push_str(&scalar_from(val).as_i64().to_string()),
                    'f' | 'g' => out.push_str(&format!("{}", scalar_from(val).as_f64())),
                    'c' => {
                        let code = scalar_from(val).as_i64();
                        if let Some(c) = char::from_u32(code as u32) {
                            out.push(c);
                        }
                    }
                    's' => out.push_str("(str)"),
                    'p' => out.push_str("(ptr)"),
                    _ => {
                        out.push('%');
                        out.push(spec);
                    }
                }
            } else {
                out.push(chars[i]);
                i += 1;
            }
        }
        self.stdout.push_str(&out);
        Ok(RValue::Scalar(Scalar::Int(out.len() as i64)))
    }

    // ---- lvalues / locations ----------------------------------------------

    fn lvalue_of(&mut self, expr: &Expr) -> Result<Location, RuntimeError> {
        match expr {
            Expr::Ident(name) => {
                let frame = self.find_var_frame(name).ok_or(RuntimeError {
                    message: format!("use of undeclared variable '{}'", name),
                    line: 0,
                })?;
                Ok(Location::Local { frame, name: name.clone() })
            }
            Expr::Index(base, idx) => self.lvalue_of_index(base, idx),
            Expr::Member { .. } => self.lvalue_of_member(expr),
            Expr::Unary(UnOp::Deref, inner) => {
                let v = self.eval_expr(inner)?;
                match v {
                    RValue::Pointer(Some(loc)) => Ok(loc),
                    RValue::Pointer(None) => Err(RuntimeError {
                        message: "cannot assign through a null pointer".into(),
                        line: 0,
                    }),
                    _ => Err(RuntimeError {
                        message: "cannot assign through a null/invalid pointer".into(),
                        line: 0,
                    }),
                }
            }
            _ => Err(RuntimeError {
                message: "invalid assignment target".into(),
                line: 0,
            }),
        }
    }

    fn lvalue_of_index(&mut self, base: &Expr, idx: &Expr) -> Result<Location, RuntimeError> {
        let index = self.eval_scalar(idx)?.as_i64();
        if index < 0 {
            return Err(RuntimeError {
                message: "negative array index".into(),
                line: 0,
            });
        }
        // The base must resolve to an array/heap block.
        let id = match base {
            Expr::Ident(name) => {
                let frame = self.find_var_frame(name).ok_or(RuntimeError {
                    message: format!("use of undeclared variable '{}'", name),
                    line: 0,
                })?;
                match self.frames[frame].slots.get(name) {
                    Some(Slot::ArrayRef { id, .. }) => id.clone(),
                    Some(Slot::Pointer(Some(Location::HeapCell { id, .. }))) => id.clone(),
                    _ => {
                        return Err(RuntimeError {
                            message: format!("'{}' is not an array or pointer", name),
                            line: 0,
                        })
                    }
                }
            }
            _ => {
                let v = self.eval_expr(base)?;
                match v {
                    RValue::Pointer(Some(Location::HeapCell { id, .. })) => id,
                    _ => {
                        return Err(RuntimeError {
                            message: "indexing a non-array expression".into(),
                            line: 0,
                        })
                    }
                }
            }
        };

        let len = match self.heap.get(&id) {
            Some(HeapObjectRuntime::Array(a)) => a.cells.len(),
            _ => 0,
        };
        if (index as usize) >= len {
            return Err(RuntimeError {
                message: format!("array index {} out of bounds (len {})", index, len),
                line: 0,
            });
        }
        Ok(Location::HeapCell { id, index: index as usize })
    }

    /// Resolve a `base.field` / `base->field` expression to a HeapField
    /// location identifying (struct id, field name). For `->`, the base is a
    /// pointer we dereference; for `.`, the base is a struct value/lvalue that
    /// must resolve to a heap struct.
    fn lvalue_of_member(&mut self, expr: &Expr) -> Result<Location, RuntimeError> {
        let (base, field, arrow) = match expr {
            Expr::Member { base, field, arrow } => (base, field.clone(), *arrow),
            _ => {
                return Err(RuntimeError {
                    message: "not a member access".into(),
                    line: 0,
                })
            }
        };

        let id = if arrow {
            // p->field : p is a pointer to a struct.
            let v = self.eval_expr(base)?;
            match v {
                RValue::Pointer(Some(Location::HeapObj { id })) => id,
                RValue::Pointer(Some(Location::HeapField { id, .. })) => id,
                RValue::Pointer(None) => {
                    return Err(RuntimeError {
                        message: "dereferenced a null pointer (->)".into(),
                        line: 0,
                    })
                }
                _ => {
                    return Err(RuntimeError {
                        message: "left of -> is not a struct pointer".into(),
                        line: 0,
                    })
                }
            }
        } else {
            // s.field : s must resolve to a heap struct object.
            let loc = self.lvalue_of(base)?;
            match loc {
                Location::HeapObj { id } => id,
                Location::Local { frame, name } => {
                    // The variable holds a pointer to a heap struct (we model
                    // struct values via heap objects).
                    match self.frames[frame].slots.get(&name) {
                        Some(Slot::Pointer(Some(Location::HeapObj { id }))) => id.clone(),
                        _ => {
                            return Err(RuntimeError {
                                message: "left of . is not a struct".into(),
                                line: 0,
                            })
                        }
                    }
                }
                _ => {
                    return Err(RuntimeError {
                        message: "left of . is not a struct".into(),
                        line: 0,
                    })
                }
            }
        };

        // Validate the field exists.
        match self.heap.get(&id) {
            Some(HeapObjectRuntime::Struct(s)) if s.field(&field).is_some() => {}
            Some(HeapObjectRuntime::Struct(s)) => {
                return Err(RuntimeError {
                    message: format!("struct '{}' has no field '{}'", s.type_name, field),
                    line: 0,
                })
            }
            _ => {
                return Err(RuntimeError {
                    message: "member access on a non-struct heap object".into(),
                    line: 0,
                })
            }
        }
        Ok(Location::HeapField { id, field })
    }

    /// If `target` is (or declares) a pointer to a struct type, return the
    /// struct's type name. Used to type a `target = malloc(...)`.
    fn struct_type_of_target(&self, target: &Expr) -> Option<String> {
        match target {
            Expr::Ident(name) => {
                let frame = self.find_var_frame(name)?;
                match self.frames[frame].declared.get(name) {
                    Some(CType { base: BaseType::Struct(s), pointer_depth }) if *pointer_depth > 0 => {
                        Some(s.clone())
                    }
                    _ => None,
                }
            }
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    fn read_location(&mut self, loc: &Location) -> Result<RValue, RuntimeError> {
        match loc {
            Location::Local { frame, name } => match self.frames[*frame].slots.get(name) {
                Some(Slot::Scalar(s)) => Ok(RValue::Scalar(s.clone())),
                Some(Slot::Pointer(p)) => Ok(RValue::Pointer(p.clone())),
                Some(Slot::ArrayRef { id, .. }) => {
                    Ok(RValue::Pointer(Some(Location::HeapCell { id: id.clone(), index: 0 })))
                }
                None => Err(RuntimeError {
                    message: format!("variable '{}' not found", name),
                    line: 0,
                }),
            },
            Location::HeapCell { id, index } => match self.heap.get(id) {
                Some(HeapObjectRuntime::Array(arr)) => {
                    Ok(RValue::Scalar(arr.cells[*index].clone()))
                }
                _ => Err(RuntimeError {
                    message: "dangling heap reference".into(),
                    line: 0,
                }),
            },
            Location::HeapField { id, field } => match self.heap.get(id) {
                Some(HeapObjectRuntime::Struct(s)) => match s.field(field) {
                    Some(Slot::Scalar(sc)) => Ok(RValue::Scalar(sc.clone())),
                    Some(Slot::Pointer(p)) => Ok(RValue::Pointer(p.clone())),
                    Some(Slot::ArrayRef { id, .. }) => Ok(RValue::Pointer(Some(
                        Location::HeapCell { id: id.clone(), index: 0 },
                    ))),
                    None => Err(RuntimeError {
                        message: format!("struct field '{}' not found", field),
                        line: 0,
                    }),
                },
                _ => Err(RuntimeError {
                    message: "field read on a non-struct heap object".into(),
                    line: 0,
                }),
            },
            Location::HeapObj { id } => {
                // Reading "the struct itself" yields a pointer to it.
                Ok(RValue::Pointer(Some(Location::HeapObj { id: id.clone() })))
            }
        }
    }

    fn write_location(&mut self, loc: &Location, value: RValue) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        match loc {
            Location::Local { frame, name } => {
                let existing = self.frames[*frame].slots.get(name).cloned();
                let new_slot = match (existing, value) {
                    (Some(Slot::Pointer(_)), RValue::Pointer(p)) => Slot::Pointer(p),
                    (_, RValue::Pointer(p)) => Slot::Pointer(p),
                    (Some(Slot::Scalar(old)), RValue::Scalar(s)) => {
                        // Preserve the slot's scalar kind where sensible.
                        Slot::Scalar(coerce_to_kind(s, &old))
                    }
                    (_, RValue::Scalar(s)) => Slot::Scalar(s),
                    (Some(prev), RValue::Void) => prev,
                    (None, RValue::Void) => Slot::Scalar(Scalar::Int(0)),
                };
                self.frames[*frame].slots.insert(name.clone(), new_slot);
                Ok(())
            }
            Location::HeapCell { id, index } => {
                let arr = match self.heap.get_mut(id) {
                    Some(HeapObjectRuntime::Array(arr)) => arr,
                    _ => {
                        return Err(RuntimeError {
                            message: "write to dangling heap reference".into(),
                            line: 0,
                        })
                    }
                };
                let elem_kind = arr.element_type.clone();
                let s = match value {
                    RValue::Scalar(s) => coerce_scalar(s, &elem_kind),
                    _ => default_scalar(&elem_kind),
                };
                arr.cells[*index] = s;
                Ok(())
            }
            Location::HeapField { id, field } => {
                let s = match self.heap.get_mut(id) {
                    Some(HeapObjectRuntime::Struct(s)) => s,
                    _ => {
                        return Err(RuntimeError {
                            message: "write to a non-struct heap object".into(),
                            line: 0,
                        })
                    }
                };
                let slot = s.field_mut(field).ok_or(RuntimeError {
                    message: format!("struct field '{}' not found", field),
                    line: 0,
                })?;
                let new_slot = match value {
                    RValue::Pointer(p) => Slot::Pointer(p),
                    RValue::Scalar(sc) => match slot {
                        Slot::Scalar(old) => Slot::Scalar(coerce_to_kind(sc, old)),
                        _ => Slot::Scalar(sc),
                    },
                    RValue::Void => return Ok(()),
                };
                *slot = new_slot;
                Ok(())
            }
            Location::HeapObj { .. } => {
                // Assigning to a whole struct object isn't modeled; ignore.
                Ok(())
            }
        }
    }

    fn read_ident(&mut self, name: &str) -> Result<RValue, RuntimeError> {
        let frame = self.find_var_frame(name).ok_or(RuntimeError {
            message: format!("use of undeclared variable '{}'", name),
            line: 0,
        })?;
        self.read_location(&Location::Local { frame, name: name.to_string() })
    }

    /// Find the frame index that declares `name`, searching the current frame
    /// only (C has no closures; globals are not modeled here).
    fn find_var_frame(&self, name: &str) -> Option<usize> {
        let top = self.frames.len().checked_sub(1)?;
        if self.frames[top].slots.contains_key(name) {
            Some(top)
        } else {
            None
        }
    }

    // ---- snapshotting -----------------------------------------------------

    /// Stable id for the frame at index `fi` (must match the id used when
    /// building the StackFrame so pointer arrows resolve to the right row).
    fn frame_id(&self, fi: usize) -> String {
        let name = self
            .frames
            .get(fi)
            .map(|f| f.function_name.as_str())
            .unwrap_or("?");
        format!("frame_{}_{}", fi, name)
    }

    /// Convert a pointer slot into a trace Value, resolving its target to a
    /// heap object or a stack variable slot (so the arrow layer can draw it).
    fn pointer_to_value(&self, p: &Option<Location>) -> TValue {
        match p {
            Some(Location::HeapCell { id, .. }) => TValue::heap_ref(id.clone()),
            Some(Location::HeapField { id, .. }) => TValue::heap_ref(id.clone()),
            Some(Location::HeapObj { id }) => TValue::heap_ref(id.clone()),
            Some(Location::Local { frame, name }) => {
                TValue::stack_ref(self.frame_id(*frame), name.clone())
            }
            None => TValue::reference(None),
        }
    }

    fn snapshot(&mut self, line: Option<usize>, note: Option<String>) {
        let step = self.states.len();

        // Build stack frames for the trace.
        let mut stack = Vec::new();
        let top = self.frames.len().saturating_sub(1);

    /// "lex" | "parse" | "runtime".
    pub stage: &'static str,
    pub message: String,
    pub line: Option<usize>,
    /// Machine-readable classification so the tutor can pick a hint sequence
    /// without re-parsing the human message. See `classify_runtime`.
    pub kind: &'static str,
}

/// Classify a lexer error message into a stable `kind` the tutor keys on.
fn classify_lex(message: &str) -> &'static str {
    if message.contains("unexpected character") {
        "lex_unexpected_char"
    } else if message.contains("unterminated string") {
        "lex_unterminated_string"
    } else if message.contains("unterminated char") || message.contains("unterminated escape") {
        "lex_unterminated_char"
    } else if message.contains("invalid integer") || message.contains("invalid float") {
        "lex_invalid_number"
    } else {
        "lex_error"
    }
}

/// Classify a parser error message into a stable `kind` the tutor keys on.
/// The parser's messages are stable, so substring matching is reliable.
fn classify_parse(message: &str) -> &'static str {
    // Specific "expected X, found Y" cases first.
    if message.contains("expected Semicolon") {
        "parse_missing_semicolon"
    } else if message.contains("expected RParen") {
        "parse_missing_rparen"
    } else if message.contains("expected LParen") {
        "parse_missing_lparen"
    } else if message.contains("expected RBrace") {
        "parse_missing_rbrace"
    } else if message.contains("expected LBrace") {
        "parse_missing_lbrace"
    } else if message.contains("expected RBracket") {
        "parse_missing_rbracket"
    } else if message.contains("expected identifier") {
        "parse_expected_identifier"
    } else if message.contains("expected a type") {
        "parse_expected_type"
    } else if message.contains("unexpected token in expression") {
        "parse_unexpected_in_expr"
    } else {
        "parse_error"
    }
}

/// Classify a runtime error message into a stable `kind` the tutor keys on.
/// Messages are produced by the interpreter and are stable, so matching on
/// substrings here is reliable.
fn classify_runtime(message: &str) -> &'static str {
    if message.contains("out of bounds") {
        "index_out_of_bounds"
    } else if message.contains("negative array index") {
        "negative_index"
    } else if message.contains("division by zero") {
        "division_by_zero"
    } else if message.contains("modulo by zero") {
        "modulo_by_zero"
    } else if message.contains("null pointer") {
        "null_deref"
    } else if message.contains("null/invalid pointer") {
        "null_deref"
    } else if message.contains("undeclared variable") {
        "undeclared_variable"
    } else if message.contains("unknown function") {
        "unknown_function"
    } else if message.contains("recursion too deep")
        || message.contains("call stack overflow")
    {
        "stack_overflow"
    } else if message.contains("infinite loop") || message.contains("step limit") {
        "infinite_loop"
    } else if message.contains("no 'main'") {
        "no_main"
    } else {
        "runtime_other"
    }
}

/// Lex, parse, and interpret a C program, producing an execution trace.
pub fn run(source: &str) -> Result<ExecutionTrace, CError> {
    let tokens = lexer::lex(source).map_err(|e| CError {
        stage: "lex",
        kind: classify_lex(&e.message),
        message: e.message,
        line: Some(e.line),
    })?;

    let mut parser = parser::Parser::new(tokens);
    let program = parser.parse_program().map_err(|e| CError {
        stage: "parse",
        kind: classify_parse(&e.message),
        message: e.message,
        line: Some(e.line),
    })?;

    let interp = interp::Interp::new(&program);
    interp.run().map_err(|e| CError {
        stage: "runtime",
        kind: classify_runtime(&e.message),
        message: e.message,
        line: if e.line == 0 { None } else { Some(e.line) },

    }

fn decode_escape(c: char) -> char {
    match c {
        'n' => '\n',
        't' => '\t',
        'r' => '\r',
        '0' => '\0',
        '\\' => '\\',
        '\'' => '\'',
        '"' => '"',
        other => other,
    }
}

# TraceLab local execution protocol (v1)
The Rust service listens only on `127.0.0.1:4317`. API calls except health require `X-TraceLab-Client: browser-v1`. This header and strict host/origin checks reduce drive-by browser requests; they are not authentication or an execution sandbox.
## Endpoints
`GET /api/health` returns runner availability and mode.
`POST /api/runs` accepts:
```json
{
  "files": [
    {"name": "Main.java", "content": "public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { System.out.println(42); } }"}
  ],
  "mainClass": "Main",
  "stdin": "",
  "maxSteps": 500,
  "timeoutMs": 15000,
  "mode": "trace",
  "startAt": {"file": "Main.java", "line": 12, "condition": "i == 25 && total > 100", "hit": 1}
}
```
`startAt` is optional and applies to `trace` mode only (other modes ignore it). `file` must be one of the request's files, `line` is 1ΓÇô100,000, `hit` (default 1) is 1ΓÇô1,000,000, and `condition` (default empty) is one line of at most 200 characters. The runner passes it to the worker as `start.txt` in the job directory (file, line, hit and condition on four lines). Until the start point fires, only breakpoints on that line are enabled (method entry/exit and the other line breakpoints are created but stay off), so the program runs at nearly full speed; nothing before it counts against `maxSteps`. It fires the `hit`-th time the line is about to run with the condition true; the frames already on the stack then get fresh activation IDs, and recording continues as usual. A line with no code moves to the next line with code in the same method (or, on a method's signature line, its first statement). An uncaught exception before the start point is recorded where it happens. A condition that can't be parsed ends the run with stop reason `bad-start` before compiling.
Condition grammar: `||`, `&&`, `!`, comparisons (`== != < <= > >=`), `+ - * / %`, unary minus, parentheses, numbers, `'c'`, `"text"`, `true`, `false`, `null`, names, `.field`, `.length` (arrays), `[index]`, and `.size()`, `.isEmpty()`, `.length()` (strings and the collections with views below). Names resolve to the paused frame's locals, then fields of `this`, then static fields of the frame's class, then user class names (for `Main.count`). Strings compare by text and boxed numbers by value. Evaluation reads values only. A name that isn't visible or an index out of range makes the condition false, and the first such problem is reported.
`mode` is optional:
- `trace` (default): compile, then run under JDI and record every step.
- `run`: compile, then run on a plain JVM with the same input, output, heap and time limits, without recording (about twice as fast). The `terminated` event has `recorded: false` and `steps: 0`. An uncaught exception is parsed from the JVM's `Exception in thread ΓÇª` line into `exception: {type, message, caught: false}` with stop reason `exception`. A program that exceeds the output limit is stopped immediately with stop reason `output-limit`. Used for tests and test generation.
- `compile`: compile only. The run ends with stop reason `compiled` or `compile-error`. Used to check suggested compile fixes.
It returns `{"id":"<opaque run id>"}` immediately. A busy runner returns HTTP 409. Paths are validated relative `.java` paths; entry classes are dot-separated Java identifiers. Requests are limited to 20 files, 64 KiB per file, 256 KiB total source, 16 KiB input and a 512 KiB JSON body.
`GET /api/runs/{id}?since=N` returns `{id,status,request,since,total,events}`. Status is `running` or `finished`. The immutable request is the exact source/input/configuration used for that run. Events are ordered by a monotonically increasing `sequence`; `events` contains only events with `sequence >= since` (default 0), and `total` is the number recorded so far. The browser polls with `since` set to the number of events it already holds, so each event is transferred once. A run is complete when `status` is `finished` and the client holds `total` events.
`DELETE /api/runs/{id}` requests cancellation. The worker observes a cancellation sentinel. The Rust supervisor force-stops the process tree if the worker does not respond promptly. Existing trace events remain readable.
## Trace events
Every event has `schemaVersion: 1`, `runId`, `sequence`, and `kind`.
- `status`: a human-readable progress `message`.
- `diagnostic`: `severity`, relative `file`, one-based `line`/`column`, and compiler `message`.
- `line`: `location: {file,line,phase:"before"}`, `threadId`, `frames`, `statics`, `heap`, capture truncation flags, and optional `returns`.
- `returns` (on `line`/`exception`): user methods that completed normally since the previous stop, oldest first: `{method, frameId, value}` or `{method, frameId, void: true}`. `frameId` matches the activation's frame `id`. Constructors and static initializers are omitted; methods exited by an exception produce no entry (JDWP does not report those exits).
- `exception`: the same captured state, plus `exception: {type,message,caught}`. For a library exception, location is the nearest user-source frame; do not present it as the exact internal library throw location.
- `output`: `stream` (`stdout` or `stderr`) and a text chunk. Receipt order is preserved, not exact source-line synchronization.
- `terminated`: `stopReason`, `message`, and, when available, `steps`, `exitCode`, `outputTruncated`, `recorded` (false in `run` mode), `exception` (`run` mode only) and `start` (when the request had `startAt`): `{reached, file, line, message?}`. `line` is the line where recording started (after moving off a line without code); when `reached` is false, `message` says why: the file's classes never loaded, the line has no code, the line never ran, or it ran N times without the condition being true (with the first evaluation problem, such as a name that isn't visible).
Stop reasons: `completed`, `compile-error`, `exception`, `runtime-error`, `step-limit`, `timeout`, `cancelled`, `unsupported-concurrency`, `trace-limit`, `worker-error`, `bad-start`, and, outside `trace` mode, `output-limit` (`run`) and `compiled` (`compile`).
Frames contain `id`, `method`, source `file`/`line`, typed `locals` (parameters carry `argument: true`), and an optional `truncated` flag. IDs are derived from method entry/exit activation tracking; after a caught exception unwinds frames, the worker realigns its activation stack with the real user frames at the next stop, so surviving frames keep their IDs. Objects use JDI identity, scoped to the run, so two references to the same object point to the same heap node. Objects are not pinned alive across stops (returned objects are pinned only until the next stop describes them). Trace data does not invoke methods on target objects. Exceptions that are thrown and caught entirely inside library code are not recorded.
Values are tagged:
```json
{"kind":"primitive","type":"int","value":"42"}
{"kind":"null","value":"null"}
{"kind":"reference","type":"int[]","ref":"o453"}
```
A reference with `omitted: true` was not traversed because of a capture budget. Objects have `id`, `type`, `kind`, and `elements`, `entries`, `fields`, `text`, or an explanatory `message`. Budgets per step: 48 frames, 32 locals per frame, 160 objects, 48 traversal levels, 64 elements or entries per collection, 24 fields per object, 32 statics, 64 pending returns, 512 characters of text; the runner stops a trace at 40 MiB. Capture kinds:
- `array`, `list` (`ArrayList`, `LinkedList`, `ArrayDeque` headΓåÆtail, `PriorityQueue` in internal heap order, `Stack`/`Vector`, `Arrays.asList`, `List.of`, `subList`, `Collections.emptyList`/`singletonList`, a map's `values()`) and `set` (`HashSet`, `LinkedHashSet`, `TreeSet`, `Set.of`, `EnumSet`, a map's `keySet()`, and `BitSet` as the indexes of its set bits): `length` plus up to 64 `elements`.
- Primitive arrays travel in a compact form: `elementType` (such as `int`) and `values` (the elements as text) instead of `elements`. Clients expand them into `{kind: "primitive", type, value}` elements on receipt (`expandEvents` in `web/learning.ts`).
- `map` (`HashMap`, `LinkedHashMap` in insertion order, `TreeMap` in key order, `Map.of`, `EnumMap`, a map's `entrySet()`): `length` plus up to 64 `entries: [{key, value}]`. A single `Map.Entry` (from iterating `entrySet()`) is a `map` with one entry and no `length`.
- `string`: `java.lang.String`, plus `StringBuilder`/`StringBuffer` decoded from their internal buffer (`length` is the logical length).
- `value`: an immutable library value shown as `text`: `java.time` types (`LocalDate`, `LocalTime`, `LocalDateTime`, `Instant`, `Duration`, `Period`, `YearMonth`, `Year`, `ZonedDateTime`, `OffsetDateTime`, zones) as their `toString()`, `AtomicInteger`/`AtomicLong`/`AtomicBoolean`, `BigInteger`, `BigDecimal`, `UUID`, `OptionalInt`/`OptionalLong`/`OptionalDouble`, and constants of JDK enums by name. The text is rebuilt from fields with the worker's own JDK classes, not by calling methods on the target.
- `object` (user classes and boxed primitives), `opaque` (other library types), and `unavailable`. Iterators of `ArrayList`, `LinkedList`, `ArrayDeque`, `HashMap`, `LinkedHashMap` and `TreeMap` are `object`s with synthetic fields `iterator.over` (the collection), `iterator.next` (what `next()` returns, if anything) and, for lists, `iterator.nextIndex`. `Optional` is an `object` with one `java.util.Optional.value` field, or none and a message when empty.
Collection views are read from JDK fields, never by calling `size()`, `iterator()` or `toString()`. If a JDK's internal layout differs from what the worker expects, the object falls back to `opaque` instead of failing the trace.
## Method-call tests
The runner has no special endpoint for these. The browser adds a generated `TraceLabCall__.java` to the request's files, in the target class's package, and sets `mainClass` to it. Its `main` evaluates the test's expression, catches any `Throwable`, and prints one line prefixed by U+001E and `TRACELAB_RESULT `: `value <formatted value>` or `throws <exception class>`. Strings and chars are printed as literals, arrays and collections element by element; other objects use `String.valueOf`, so this is the one place student `toString()` methods can run. The harness file is excluded when comparing a run with the project's source. Requests still count against the 20-file limit.
A call is split at top-level semicolons (outside strings, chars and brackets). One piece is an expression and is evaluated as is. Statements followed by an expression run inside a lambda, `((Thunk__) () -> { statements; return expression; }).get()`. Statements ending in `;` run inside `printed__`, which swaps `System.out` for a buffer while they run and returns what they printed, with `\r\n` turned into `\n` and trailing whitespace removed, as a `String` value. A leading bare call in each statement is qualified with the target class.

**All three use Rust + TypeScript at a surface level, but they are three incompatible applications — not three backends behind one UI.** Specifically:

| | **Your C branch** | **Java branch** | **Python branch** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Backend | Hand-written interpreter, sync `POST /api/run` → one `ExecutionTrace` | `tracelab-server`: real JVM + JDI + JDTLS, async `POST /api/runs` + polling on **:4317**, custom headers | `kiro-server`: shells out to **`tracer.py`** (the Python Tutor / `pg_logger` engine), `POST /api/run-code` |
| Trace schema | Your `{states:[{stack,heap,...}]}`, tagged `Value`/`HeapObject` | `schemaVersion:1` event stream (`line`/`output`/`terminated`), `{"kind":"reference","ref":"o453"}` | Python Tutor's `pg_logger` encoding — arrays like `["REF", 5]`, `["INSTANCE", ...]` |
| Frontend | React `.tsx`, your components | **Plain TS** (`web/*.ts`), no React | React `.tsx`, but totally different components (`MemoryView`, `QuizCard`) |
| External deps | None | Java JDK + JDTLS | Python + tracer.py |

So the three traces are mutually unintelligible, the Java one isn't even React, and two require external runtimes (JDK, Python). "Click the dropdown and the Java branch's code kicks in" is genuinely hard, because there's no shared contract anywhere.

Given that, here are your realistic options, from most-honest-to-the-constraints to most-ambitious:

**Option 1 — Separate apps, unified by a launcher/links (low effort, honest).** Keep all three apps as-is. The dropdown doesn't swap interpreters in-place; instead each language launches/links to its own app (each running on its own port). You present it as "CodeTrace: three language tracers." No deep integration, nothing breaks, and it's achievable before a deadline. The dropdown becomes a navigation control.

**Option 2 — Your frontend, three backends via adapters (high effort).** Keep *your* React UI as the single frontend. For each language, write an **adapter** that calls that teammate's backend and translates its trace into *your* `ExecutionTrace` schema so your visualizer can render it. This is real work per language — the Java event-stream→your-schema adapter alone is substantial, and you'd need to run the JVM/Python backends alongside yours. The dropdown would then truly drive one UI. This is the "right" architecture but it's easily the biggest task in the whole project, and it depends on your teammates' backends being runnable on the demo machine (JDK, Python installed).

**Option 3 — Reimplement Java/Python as interpreters in *your* backend (very high effort).** Mirror what you did for C — hand-write Java and Python interpreters emitting your trace format. Clean and self-contained, but that's essentially rebuilding your teammates' work; not realistic in remaining time.

**My honest recommendation: Option 1 for the hackathon**, with Option 2 as the "if we have lots of time" stretch. The reason is blunt — your teammates built standalone apps with different protocols, schemas, external runtime dependencies, and (for Java) a different frontend framework. Forcing them into one in-place UI is a large systems-integration effort that can't be done cleanly or quickly, and it risks breaking three working demos right before judging.

Two things before I'd build anything:
1. **This affects your teammates' code and how you all present.** This is a team decision, not just a merge. Worth a quick sync with them on whether the goal is "one unified UI" (Option 2, big lift, needs their buy-in and their backends adapted) or "one entry point that launches three apps" (Option 1).

# TraceLab
TraceLab is a Java IDE in the browser with a recording debugger and a built-in tutor. It runs your program on a real JVM, records every step, and lets you move forward and back through the call stack and heap. The Tutor asks questions drawn from your own run, then checks your fix against tests.

# CodeTrace Python Visualizer

objects, pointers), and has Kiro, a Socratic AI tutor, quiz you about the exact state you're paused on.

| Tracing | Python 3.11+ running pg_logger from OnlinePythonTutor | `tracer.py`, `pg_logger.py`, `pg_encoder.py` |

```powershell
.\run.cmd
```

  the Rust build needs. `run.ps1` finds all three.

  and any `None` pointer the current line reads through.

import { existsSync, readdirSync, mkdirSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join, resolve } from 'node:path';
import { spawn, spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

export const root = resolve(fileURLToPath(new URL('..', import.meta.url)));
process.chdir(root);
export const windows = process.platform === 'win32';
const exe = (name) => name + (windows ? '.exe' : '');

export function javaHome() {
  const candidates = [process.env.TRACELAB_JAVA_HOME, process.env.JAVA_HOME];
  const extensionRoot = join(process.env.USERPROFILE || process.env.HOME || '', '.vscode', 'extensions');
  if (existsSync(extensionRoot)) {
    for (const ext of readdirSync(extensionRoot).filter(n => n.startsWith('redhat.java-')).sort().reverse()) {
      const dir = join(extensionRoot, ext, 'jre');
      if (existsSync(dir)) for (const jdk of readdirSync(dir)) candidates.push(join(dir, jdk));
    }
  }
  for (const dir of candidates.filter(Boolean)) {
    if (existsSync(join(dir, 'bin', exe('javac')))) {
      const result = spawnSync(join(dir, 'bin', exe('java')), ['-version'], { encoding: 'utf8' });
      const major = Number((result.stderr + result.stdout).match(/version "(\d+)/)?.[1]);
      if (major >= 21) return dir;
    }
  }
  const pathJavac = spawnSync(windows ? 'where.exe' : 'which', ['javac'], { encoding: 'utf8' });
  if (pathJavac.status === 0) {
    const candidate = resolve(pathJavac.stdout.trim().split(/\r?\n/)[0], '../..');
    const version = spawnSync(join(candidate, 'bin', exe('java')), ['-version'], { encoding: 'utf8' });
    if (Number((version.stderr + version.stdout).match(/version "(\d+)/)?.[1]) >= 21) return candidate;
  }
  throw new Error('A JDK 21+ is required. Set JAVA_HOME or TRACELAB_JAVA_HOME to its directory.');
}

/**
 * Eclipse JDT Language Server for editor features: TRACELAB_JDTLS_HOME, a copy downloaded by
 * `npm run setup:jdtls` into .tools/jdtls, or the one bundled with the VS Code Java extension.
 * Returns the folder that contains plugins/ and config_*, or null.
 */
export function jdtlsHome() {
  const valid = dir => dir && existsSync(join(dir, 'plugins')) && readdirSync(join(dir, 'plugins')).some(n => n.startsWith('org.eclipse.equinox.launcher_'));
  if (valid(process.env.TRACELAB_JDTLS_HOME)) return process.env.TRACELAB_JDTLS_HOME;
  if (valid(join(root, '.tools/jdtls'))) return join(root, '.tools/jdtls');
  const home = process.env.USERPROFILE || process.env.HOME || '';
  const version = name => (name.match(/(\d+)\.(\d+)\.(\d+)/) ?? []).slice(1).map(Number);
  const newer = (a, b) => { const x = version(a), y = version(b); for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) if ((x[i] ?? 0) !== (y[i] ?? 0)) return (y[i] ?? 0) - (x[i] ?? 0); return 0; };
  for (const editor of ['.vscode', '.kiro', '.vscode-insiders', '.cursor']) {
    const extensions = join(home, editor, 'extensions');
    if (!existsSync(extensions)) continue;
    for (const ext of readdirSync(extensions).filter(n => n.startsWith('redhat.java-')).sort(newer)) {
      if (valid(join(extensions, ext, 'server'))) return join(extensions, ext, 'server');
    }
  }
  return null;
}

export function environment() {
  const env = { ...process.env, JAVA_HOME: javaHome() };
  const jdtls = jdtlsHome();
  if (jdtls && process.env.TRACELAB_LANGUAGE_SERVER !== 'off') {
    env.TRACELAB_JDTLS_HOME = jdtls;
    env.TRACELAB_JDTLS_JAVA = join(env.JAVA_HOME, 'bin', exe('java'));
  } else {
    delete env.TRACELAB_JDTLS_HOME;
    delete env.TRACELAB_JDTLS_JAVA;
  }
  if (existsSync(join(root, '.tools/cargo/bin', exe('cargo')))) {
    env.CARGO_HOME = join(root, '.tools/cargo');
    env.RUSTUP_HOME = join(root, '.tools/rustup');
    env.PATH = join(root, '.tools/cargo/bin') + (windows ? ';' : ':') + env.PATH;
  }
  env.TRACELAB_ROOT = root;
  return env;
}

export function run(command, args, env = environment()) {
  return new Promise((resolvePromise, reject) => {
    const child = spawn(command, args, { cwd: root, env, stdio: 'inherit', windowsHide: true });
    child.on('error', reject);
    child.on('exit', code => code === 0 ? resolvePromise() : reject(new Error(`${command} exited with ${code}`)));
  });
}

export async function buildWorker() {
  const env = environment();
  mkdirSync(join(root, '.local/worker'), { recursive: true });

}
